text:
incident-bot: ALERT — increased 5xx and p95 latency for inference requests from region 'us-west-2a'. Auto-detected flow: controlplane -> worker-net egress errors. Paging on-call. :rotating_light:

emma_sre: I'm on it. seeing a spike in socket errors and GRPC stream resets for a subset of hosts (ephemeral pool). starting triage.

raj_oncall: joining. any obvious deploys?

maria_infra: no deploys in the last 2 hours. cloud metrics show ENI RX error bursts and resolver timeouts from the AZ. RouteHealth shows ~30% of egress paths with high RTT.

emma_sre: confirmed, logs: ```grpc: received reset from remote: EOF
2026-03-17T12:02:13Z host-az-usw2a-ephem-23 kernel: RX-ERR backlog```

product-lead: impact? are customers seeing failures or degraded throughput?

customer-ops: some customers reporting slow responses and timeouts on streaming endpoints. we've flagged 3 accounts on the public status page.

raj_oncall: quick mitigation idea: route traffic away from us-west-2a to us-west-2b/ eu-west-1 for affected models. can we flip routing policy for inference tier 'standard' to use fallback pool?

maria_infra: routing engine supports policy shift. planning to apply a soft redirect for new requests and let existing connections drain. command: ```/runbook routing shift --from=us-west-2a --to=us-west-2b --mode=soft```

emma_sre: runbook step 1 -> verify capacity in target regions: we have spare capacity in us-west-2b (40% idle). step 2 -> apply soft shift. step 3 -> monitor p50/p95 and error rates.

deployment-bot: Runbook action queued by maria_infra: routing shift initiated. Job id: rb-20260317-01.

emma_sre: applied soft shift. new session placement is now preferring us-west-2b. existing long-lived streams will drain naturally.

raj_oncall: monitoring... p95 for standard model dropped from 1.2s -> 420ms for shifted traffic. 5xx rate decreasing.

customer-ops: update posted to status page: "Investigating elevated error rates in us-west-2a impacting inference latency. Traffic being redirected to adjacent regions to mitigate impact."

product-lead: good. need a customer impact summary for downstream comms and CSMs. Emma, can you draft quick bullet points?

emma_sre: Draft: "Between 11:58–12:18 UTC we observed network egress errors in us-west-2a leading to elevated 5xx and p95 latency for inference. We mitigated by routing new requests to us-west-2b and eu-west-1; streaming sessions are draining and recovery is in progress. Some customers experienced timeouts during the window; no model data loss reported."

maria_infra: tagging network/contact to open a cloud support case for potential host-level NIC degradation. support case created: AWS-CASE-987654321.

raj_oncall: starting oncall handoff notes: cause suspected = AZ-level network egress degradation affecting ephemeral hosts; mitigation = traffic shift and region fallback; customer impact = elevated errors/timeouts for ~20 minutes for specific model routes; follow-up = cloud case + infra postmortem if host-level NIC confirmed.

emma_sre: capturing metrics snapshot and upload: ```s3://redwood-ops/incidents/7512345678/metrics_snapshot_20260317T1205.json```

deployment-bot: routing shift job rb-20260317-01 completed successfully. All new placements now prefer fallback regions.

maria_infra: resolver caches were also noisy — TTLs spiked which magnified egress load. We flushed local resolver caches and applied transient backoff to upstream queries.

product-lead: next steps for post-incident: 1) confirm AWS case outcome, 2) add an automated traffic-splay when per-AZ egress RTT exceeds threshold, 3) run a tabletop for cross-region failover.

customer-ops: CSMs notified. customers asked to reach out if they still see issues — none reported after 12:25 UTC.

emma_sre: preparing handoff to night oncall. If anything regresses, please escalate pager and re-run the routing shift to force immediate placement.

raj_oncall: handing off. Handoff note: incident resolved to mitigation state at 12:22 UTC; monitor until 13:00 UTC for regression.

incident-bot: INCIDENT_UPDATE — severity: SEV3 -> mitigated. Timeline: detected 11:58 UTC, mitigated (soft routing) 12:05 UTC, stabilized 12:22 UTC.

maria_infra: AWS support acknowledged packet drop trend and marked as "networking degrade" in us-west-2a. They'll provide logs and possible host replacement timeline.

emma_sre: thanks team. I'll open a postmortem draft and include suggested runbook additions (automatic splay + faster resolver flush).

product-lead: great work. :thumbsup:

raj_oncall: logging final metrics and closing thread.

emma_sre: thread closed for handoff.
